label: Stop 1: Het Steen and the Scheldt riverfront

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Where are we?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On the riverbank, beside the Scheldt.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The wide brown river in front of you is the reason this city exists.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's not very blue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a working river. Blue is not its job.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And that small stone building behind us?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's Het Steen. The name means, roughly, the Stone.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look at the gateway, the arched part by the bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was built between 1200 and 1225.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's older than almost everything we'll see today.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Older than the town hall, older than the cathedral's tower, older than the printing houses.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: People say it's the oldest building in Antwerp.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll say by some counts.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why the hedge?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Because the whole site is older than the gateway.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There was a settlement and a fortification here by the 9th century.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The gateway is what survives of a bigger castle of the Dukes of Brabant.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The rest was torn down in the 19th century.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's the one piece left.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The front door. Then around 1520 it was rebuilt under Emperor Charles V, and that's when the name Het Steen took hold.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what did they use it for?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Many things. A place for the city's aldermen and a court of justice.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And from 1303 to 1827, a prison.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's over 500 years of prison.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Then an archaeology museum from 1890, and a maritime museum annex from 1952.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: After a big renovation that finished in October 2021, it reopened as a visitor center, with a modern concrete extension.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Can we go in?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's worth checking. It works as a gateway for visitors now.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But for this walk, the outside is enough.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Now look at the bridge. There's a statue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A giant. That's Lange Wapper.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is that the giant from the legend?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not quite. Different giant. Lange Wapper is a figure from local folklore who is said to have terrorized the medieval townspeople.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He's not the one with the toll.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: There's more than one giant?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a big city. Now, the giant with the toll.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is where the city's name story starts.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The hand. The legend says a giant called Druoon Antigoon lived by the Scheldt, right about here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Any ship that wanted to pass had to pay a toll.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And if you didn't pay?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He cut off your hand.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Charming man.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then a hero named Brabo came along.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He fought the giant, cut off his hand, and threw it into the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's one hand, in the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: My tally says one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Hold the tally. The story says that's how the city got its name.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Hand throwing. Whether that's true, nobody knows.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But the city likes the story so much that it keeps telling it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A city founded on a throw.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A good throw.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the river itself. How big a deal was it?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Enormous. About 1500, the channel to the old trading city of Bruges silted up.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Foreign merchants moved their trading houses here, because Antwerp's river was deep.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So this spot was the front door of a trade empire.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: For a while. By 1560, Antwerp was the second-largest city in Europe north of the Alps.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And then came the Spanish Fury in 1576, a siege in 1585, and in 1648 the river itself was closed to shipping by a treaty.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll hear about the Fury in a minute, at the town hall.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What happened to the river afterward?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Napoleon eased the restrictions and built docks.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The last restriction ended in 1863.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Today Antwerp is one of the major seaports in the world, which is a nice kind of revenge.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the river made it, broke it, and made it again.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the whole city in one sentence.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Time to pause. Look at the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Look at the gateway. Find the giant by the bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: When you're ready, here is the way on.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Turn your back to the water and look for the street that runs straight inland from the square, the Suikerrui.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It leads toward the church towers.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A few minutes' walk, a little uphill, and it opens into the main square.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is that the one with the fountain?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. And the fountain has Brabo on top, holding up something.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh no. Is it the hand?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll get there.
